transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 09:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sonia Patel (Redwood AE); Marco Reyes (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (BrightCart Eng Mgr); Luke Moran (BrightCart ML Eng); Dana Cho (BrightCart Platform); Eric Holt (BrightCart Product)

[00:00] Sonia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check are we all good on time?
[00:06] Priya (BrightCart): Yep, sounds good, we have about an hour, thanks.
[00:10] Sonia: Cool. Agenda: pick anchor model, review quantized compatibility tests, define pinning semantics, and run a short tabletop cutover. Marco, I'll hand to you for the technical details.
[00:20] Marco (Redwood SE): Thanks. Quick reminder of the workload: checkout ranking, avg request length is short, 30-60 tokens, very spiky during sales events. BrightCart's p95 latency target is 120ms for user-visible calls, right?
[00:28] Priya: Yes, 120ms p95 is the threshold. If we go over during peak, product will not accept it.
[00:33] Luke: Also we want deterministic outputs across pins — we can't have large drift between versions, that breaks our business logic.
[00:40] Marco: Right. So option A is anchor on the 13B dense open model (non-quant), option B is anchor on the 13B q8 variant with a soft-hedge to a lower-cost distilled 7B for burst. Option C is dedicated small family - keep prod on a hosted non-quant but reserve dedicated capacity for spikes.
[00:53] Eric (BrightCart): I like option B on cost grounds but worried about determinism and small result regressions when switching models.
[00:58] Marco: That's the key tradeoff — quantization + kernel differences can change tokenization or rounding on logits causing subtle behavior changes. We ran initial QA on 500 prompts; drift was low for top-1 but some rerank order flips at the tail.
[01:12] Luke: Can you share which prompts flipped? We need to see business-sensitive examples (e.g., payment-related phrasing).
[01:18] Marco: Yes, I'll dump the list — it's in the compatibility report link I posted in chat (link: https://redwood.internal/compat/BC-4981). Note, transcription: some of the file names got munged in S3, so path might be slightly different.
[01:35] Dana (Platform): On networking/security: we must have KMS integration and VPC peering by the time we go to dedicated. Also audit logs for the last 90 days are required.
[01:45] Sonia: Understood. Our Private and Dedicated options both support customer KMS and VPC peering; audit logs and extended retention are an add-on. We'll include the security docs.
[01:52] Priya: Great. Back to pinning semantics — we prefer route-level pinning for checkout API, not user-level. Simpler to roll back and test.
[01:58] Marco: Route-level pin is straightforward: you pin a route name to a model version or variant set. You can also do sticky session pins if you want same user seeing same model for short windows, but that adds state.
[02:08] Luke: For canary, can we do 10% traffic to anchor q8 and 90% to current prod for two hours and measure accuracy and latency?
[02:15] Marco: Yes, we can configure traffic slices in the routing policy. Important: when routing across model families we need to ensure schema compatibility for outputs and function-calling shapes.
[02:24] Eric: If we hit an anomaly, what is the emergency escape? Rollback route-level pin to previous version? How fast is that?
[02:32] Marco: Rollback is immediate — the control plane flips routing flags and requests start hitting the fallback within seconds. However, in-flight responses with streaming tokens may still complete on the old instance. We also recommend an automated monitor to detect regressions and trigger the rollback.
[02:46] Sonia: Today we'll do a tabletop: Marco will simulate a regression and we'll step through the rollback.
[02:50] Marco: Ok I'll narrate. Scenario: we cut 10% of checkout traffic to 13B-q8 anchor. At T+15m we see p95 jump to 180ms and a 2% drop in top-1 accuracy on the fraud-detection prompt set.
[03:05] Priya: What monitoring signals should we have before automating? p95 latency, error rate, a domain-specific metric (fraud-flag rate), and a quality delta on a small prompt set.
[03:13] Marco: Exactly. The Redwood console supports custom eval hooks — you can upload a prompt set and compute delta in real-time.
[03:20] Luke: Small question — does the eval check run on the same instances or a shadow path? We don't want it to add load.
[03:26] Marco: It can run in shadow mode; we run small sampled evals against the candidate model on lightweight instances or on the same instances if you accept the overhead. For canaries we recommend shadow evals to avoid contamination.
[03:36] Dana: For the dedicated trial, what GPUs are you provisioning? We need to match our latency numbers.
[03:41] Marco: For the q8 13B anchor we used A100-80GB in the trial; for cost reasons we can recommend an H100 or 80GB A100 fleet depending on availability. I'll put exact kernel perf numbers in the compatibility doc.
[03:53] Eric: If we go with q8 anchor plus fallback to distilled 7B, how do we handle KV cache migration? Any risk of cold cache during swap?
[04:02] Marco: Great point — switching to a different model family invalidates KV caches. For short cutover we prefer soft-hedge: route a small percentage to the jettisoned model and warm caches via shadow calls; for full cutover expect a cold-cache penalty for first requests. We'll document an eviction/warm strategy in the runbook.
[04:21] Priya: How about pins that are time-bound, e.g., pin for 2 hours then auto-unpin if no manual confirmation? Useful for trials.
[04:28] Sonia: We support TTL-based pins. You can set an expiration and require a manual extend. We'll include a sample policy.
[04:34] Luke: We also need reproducible inference across staging/prod. Can Redwood pin kernel/runtime flags so quantization behavior is consistent?
[04:42] Marco: Yes — the model variant includes runtime flags (kernel selection, flash attention variant). When you pin you lock those flags. If you do a soft-hedge to a different variant you must include acceptance of those flags.
[04:54] Eric: Can you remind us of the cost delta for 13B non-quant vs q8 vs 7B distilled? Ballpark per-1M tokens.
[04:61] Marco: (laugh) math glitch — let me give ballparks: non-quant 13B ~ $X per 1M tokens, q8 13B ~ 0.6X, 7B distilled ~ 0.25X. Exacts in pricing doc I'll share.
[05:10] Priya: Okay. Can we talk about the rollback runbook steps? We want concrete items.
[05:15] Marco: Runbook (high level): 1) Detect via monitors (p95, domain metric, eval delta), 2) Execute immediate route flip to fallback, 3) Notify on-call and trigger a postmortem job, 4) If fallback fails, kick emergency full cutover to dedicated reserved or previous AMI, 5) Run smoke tests.
[05:33] Priya: Steps 2 and 4 sound similar; what's the difference between fallback and full cutover?
[05:38] Marco: Fallback is model variant switching within the same route (e.g., q8 -> non-quant on same model family or to a pinned 7B). Full cutover might redirect to a different cluster (dedicated pool) if resource contention or regional failover required.
[05:50] Dana: From a networking perspective, cluster cutover means different peering endpoints; we need DNS TTL guidance.
[05:56] Marco: We'll recommend low TTLs (30s) during cutover window and health-check redirection.
[06:02] Sonia: Let's do the drill. Marco will mark 10% canary, simulate latency spike, then execute rollback.
[06:08] Marco: Marking canary now in the control plane — (simulated) canary traffic started. I'm seeing synthetic p95 jump in the console graph to 190ms.
[06:20] Priya: We see it on our side too. Simulated false-positive?
[06:23] Luke: The prompt-level eval shows a 2.1% drop on fraud-set.
[06:27] Marco: Rolling back — flipping route pin to previous variant now. Status: API acknowledged, traffic switching.
[06:35] Eric: Time to effective rollback?
[06:37] Marco: We're observing traffic shift within 6–12s in the console. Latency trending back down, p95 at 110ms now.
[06:45] Priya: Good. Postmortem items?
[06:48] Sonia: We'll capture the eval diffs and add to the compatibility spreadsheet, plus identify if the flips were due to quantization or tokenization differences.
[06:55] Luke: For the compatibility tests you ran — did you include our payment and internationalized prompts?
[06:59] Marco: I included a seed set but not exhaustive. Action: Marco to run a focused test on payment/internationalization.
[07:05] Priya: Also we need logs showing API keys and token-level cost by route for monthly cost forecasting.
[07:12] Sonia: Redwood Console can export token usage by route and model; we'll send an example.
[07:18] Dana: A few other compliance questions — can we do SSO/SAML for team access and restrict logs to certain roles?
[07:25] Sonia: Yes, RBAC + SAML SSO supported; audit logs can be restricted to admin roles and we can send a sample policy.
[07:31] Eric: On the dedicated trial, we also want an SLA burn-in period and to run a simulated Black Friday spike. Is that possible?
[07:38] Marco: We can provision a short burn-in and coordinate a spike test with synthetic traffic. We'll need lead time for GPU availability.
[07:45] Priya: Timeline: we want to be ready to flip in production for the mid-August feature release. So pilot must complete by early August.
[07:53] Sonia: That seems doable. Two-week dedicated trial starting next week would give you time for canary and cutover drill.
[07:59] Marco: I'll open the trial order after today's call.
[08:02] Eric: Let's document the pinning policy: route-level pin default, canary TTL 2 hours, auto-rollback thresholds: p95 > 140ms or eval delta > 1.5% on fraud set.
[08:16] Sonia: We'll draft that policy and include in the runbook.
[08:20] Luke: Quick question on drift: if a pinned model has a hotfix patch applied upstream (new tokenizer), how do we handle incremental fixes?
[08:27] Marco: You can create a new variant and pin it, then run a staged rollout. We recommend tagging variants with semantic versioning and using the console to compare diffs.
[08:36] Priya: Anything else on pin semantics? We want a UI toggle for emergency unpin.
[08:40] Sonia: There's a one-click rollback in the Console for route-level pins; we'll show it in the demo next week.
[08:45] Dana: Ops question — who has on-call for the POC? We need contacts and escalation.
[08:50] Sonia: I'll put AE/SE on the contact list for the trial; we'll include on-call rotation if you move to Dedicated.
[08:56] Eric: Can you share the compatibility CSV and pricing sketch after the call?
[09:00] Sonia: Yes — next steps: share pinning matrix, runbook, compatibility test results, and a pricing sketch. Also schedule the tabletop cutover for 2026-07-21.
[09:09] Luke: Thanks. Quick FYI — we'll confirm canary percentages by tomorrow.
[09:12] Priya: Thanks everyone. That wraps it up.
[09:15] Sonia: Thanks — end of recording.

Notes: transcript contains some ASR artifacts (times around 04:61 numeric glitch), some proper nouns mangled in later file paths. Links in chat may require sign-in.
